raw_response:
Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates lucent streaks of air outlining the mediastinal structures, particularly along the left heart border and extending into the neck (continuous diaphragm sign), which is characteristic of pneumomediastinum. This pattern, especially when prominent anteriorly and in the absence of massive pleural effusion or hydropneumothorax, is most consistent with alveolar rupture (Macklin effect) rather than esophageal perforation.
